subject.title: fix(sessions): stop cap enforcement from deleting every removable entry

question: When durable or runtime-protected session pointers already meet `session.maintenance.maxEntries`, should OpenClaw suspend count-based eviction of every removable synthetic entry, or should it retain a bounded non-destructive removable-entry policy?
rationale: Both choices alter the established meaning of an existing user configuration: the current behavior enforces a count cap destructively, while this PR removes that count-retention path in the protected-over-cap state. Repository policy treats config/default and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Adopt protected-overage retention
options.body: Accept that protected pointers override the count cap, document that synthetic entries are then retained by age and disk policies, and add after-fix runtime proof.

options.title: Preserve bounded removable retention
options.body: Define a bounded non-destructive policy for eligible entries during protected overage, document it, and cover both fresh and upgraded configurations.

options.title: Pause the behavior change
options.body: Keep the current cap semantics until an owner-approved retention policy is available.

recommendation.title: Preserve bounded removable retention
recommendation.body: Define a bounded non-destructive policy for eligible entries during protected overage, document it, and cover both fresh and upgraded configurations.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the nearest active-session preservation invariant and provides the clearest history signal for this policy boundary.
